Priya K: Customer reported function_call failing when sending args as a JSON string with a stray comma. Getting 400 parse error. Repro below.

Priya K: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model":"gpt-neo-1.3b",
  "input":"Summarize this",
  "tool_call": {
    "name":"send_email",
    "args": "{\"to\":\"user@example.com\", \"subject\":\"Hi\", }"
  }
}'
```

Sam R: Can you paste the exact error body + request_id? :eyes:

Priya K: ```json
{
  "error": "tool_args_parse_error",
  "message": "Invalid JSON in tool args: Unexpected token ',' at position 72",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "status": 400
}
```

Eng-Tooling Bot: log: parser failed for req_0a1b2c3d; ip=54.12.34.56; user_agent=customer-client/1.2.3; stack=JSON.parse -> SyntaxError: Unexpected token ,

Jordan L: Looks like client pasted JSON as a string with a trailing comma. Two options: 1) pass args as an object (preferred) or 2) ensure JSON.stringify on client. Example:

Jordan L: ```json
"tool_call": {
  "name": "send_email",
  "args": {"to":"user@example.com","subject":"Hi"}
}
```

Jordan L: or if you must send a string: ```js
"args": JSON.stringify({to: "user@example.com", subject: "Hi"})
```

Maggie S: Created ticket RINF-842 assigned to eng-runtime to add clearer error message and a docs snippet about required args types. No server-side auto-fix — sanitizing could hide other bugs. :thumbsup:

Sam R: FYI added a quick check in support playbook: look for trailing commas, smart-quotes, and Windows paste artifacts. Asking customer to patch and retest.

Priya K: Customer confirmed they fixed the client — calls now succeed. Closing unless we want follow-up documentation. :white_check_mark:
